children.text: New Zealand's government has updated its immigration visa in order to attract skilled workers. Under the changes, the cap on visas issued to highly skilled workers has been removed. Additionally, the duration of the Accredited Employer Work Visa (AEWV) has been increased from 3 to 5 years.

"The changes to the immigration visa will remove the artificial constraint on the number of places available each year for skilled workers, which prevents skilled migrants from settling in New Zealand even when there is a genuine need for them." - said New Zealand's Minister of Immigration, Michael Wood.
The minister also noted that attracting skilled migrants to the country will help develop sectors that are experiencing labor shortages.
Applicants who wish to apply for the skilled workers' immigration visa must hold a job offer from an accredited employer.
Along with having an employer's offer, it's important to confirm the relevant qualifications and skills, which are assessed under a 6-point system.
To apply for the visa, the applicant must be 55 years of age or younger.

page.title: Requirements for Skilled Workers' Immigration Visa

children.text: Identification
- it's important to confirm your identity and the identity of anyone else listed in your application.
English language
- the applicant must have a good command of the English language.
Job offer
- you must hold a job offer from New Zealand.
Qualification
- the applicant must be qualified in the relevant field.

In order for a Georgian citizen to be able to work in New Zealand, they must hold the appropriate visa category. If you're interested in the skilled workers' visa, our team will provide you with full visa support. Keep in mind that before starting the visa process, an offer from an employer and holding the relevant qualification are important requirements.
